::: {.lead}
Today you turn the book fair notice into a small report with a cover, a
header, page numbers and a table of contents. Each experiment has two
parts. **Part A** is in Word on the lab computer. **Part B** is on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box. At
the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word (the desktop app, or Word on the
  web at `office.com`).
- **Get ready:** open your notice of Lecture 7, or `book-fair-start.docx`.
  If it has no styles yet, give the first line the style **Title** and the
  four headings *When and where*, *What you can bring*, *How to swap a
  book* and *Prices* the style **Heading 1** (Home › Styles).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Word.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · The page: orientation, margins and a page break

**The idea:** **Layout › Orientation:** **Portrait** (tall, the normal page)
or **Landscape** (wide); a wide table fits better on a landscape page.
**Layout › Margins:** the empty space around the text: Normal, Narrow or
Wide; smaller margins give the text more room. A **page break** (**Ctrl +
Enter**) starts the next text on a new page, for example after a cover.
Never press Enter many times to reach a new page.

**Aim:** make a cover page, and see what the margins and the orientation
change.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Click at the end of the title line, *Book Fair at the College Library*,
   and press **Ctrl + Enter**. Look at page 1 and page 2.

   {{< record "Page 1 now has … ; the text starts on page …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Page 1 has only the title: a **cover page**. The text starts on **page
   2**. The page break keeps it there, even when the text above changes.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Omar pressed Enter 15 times to reach a new page. Later he adds a line on
   the cover. What happens?

   - [x] The empty lines move, and the text starts in the wrong place.

     Why: Empty lines move with the text; a page break (Ctrl + Enter) stays.

   - [ ] Nothing: the text stays on the new page.

     Why: Only a page break keeps the text on the new page.

   - [ ] Word changes the empty lines into a page break.

     Why: Word never does this by itself.
   :::

2. Click **Layout › Margins › Narrow**, and look at the lines of page 2.
   Then click **Layout › Orientation › Landscape**. Look at the pages, then
   set them back to **Portrait** and **Normal**.

   {{< record "Narrow margins: the lines … ; landscape: the page …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   With **Narrow** margins the lines are longer: more text fits on each
   line. With **Landscape** the page is wide: on A4 with Normal margins,
   the text is about 25 cm wide instead of about 16 cm.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="25" unit="cm" tol="1" hint="Landscape gives the text more room than the 16 cm of portrait."}
   On an A4 page with Normal margins, the text is about 16 cm wide in
   portrait. About how wide is it in landscape?

   Why: A landscape page is wide: about 25 cm of text, so a wide table fits.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/page-setup-lab.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/page-setup-lab.png" title="Page Setup Lab: orientation, margins and a page break" >}}

3. In **Page Setup Lab**, the class report has a table of six columns, 20
   cm wide. Try the orientations and the margins until the table fits.
   Then put a page break after the cover. Which setting makes the table
   fit?

   {{< record "The table fits with …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Landscape**: the text area is about 25 cm wide, so the 20 cm table
   fits. In portrait it is only about 16 cm wide (Normal margins), and even
   Narrow margins give less than 20 cm.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Page Setup Lab, the table is 20 cm wide. Which setting gives it room?

   - [x] Landscape

     Why: A landscape page has about 25 cm of text.

   - [ ] Portrait with Wide margins

     Why: Wide margins leave even less room for the text.

   - [ ] A page break before the table

     Why: A page break moves the table to a new page, but the page is just as narrow.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Header, footer and page numbers

**The idea:** the **header** is the top area of every page; the **footer**
is the bottom area. You type in them once, and the text is on every page.
**Insert › Page Number › Bottom of Page** writes the right number on every
page. A cover has no header and no number: tick **Different First Page**
(Header & Footer tab). Double-click in the text to go back.

**Aim:** put a header and page numbers on every page, but not on the cover.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Click **Insert › Header › Blank** and type *College Library · Book
   Fair*. Then click **Insert › Page Number › Bottom of Page** and choose a
   number in the middle. Double-click in the text, and look at page 1 and
   page 2.

   {{< record "The header is on page(s) … ; the numbers are …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The header is on **both pages**: you typed it once. The numbers are
   **1** and **2**, at the bottom: Word writes the right number on every
   page.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   What belongs in a header?

   - [x] the name of the document, for example College Library · Book Fair

     Why: The header repeats on every page, so it holds what every page needs.

   - [ ] the first paragraph of the notice

     Why: The text of the document goes in the page, not in the header.

   - [ ] the table of prices

     Why: A table belongs in the text of one page.
   :::

2. Double-click the header of page 1. In the **Header & Footer** tab, tick
   **Different First Page**. Double-click in the text. Look at pages 1
   and 2 again.

   {{< record "Page 1 shows … ; page 2 shows …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The cover (page 1) has **no header and no number**. Page 2 still has the
   header and the number **2**: Word keeps counting the cover.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   After you tick **Different First Page**, which number is at the bottom
   of page 2?

   - [x] 2

     Why: The cover has no number, but Word still counts it as page 1.

   - [ ] 1

     Why: Word counts every page, the cover too.

   - [ ] no number

     Why: Different First Page changes only the first page.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/header-footer-lab.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/header-footer-lab.png" title="Header and Footer Lab: on every page" >}}

3. In **Header and Footer Lab**, reach the three goals: a header on pages 2
   and 3, page numbers at the bottom of pages 2 and 3, and no header and no
   number on the cover. Which setting gives the empty cover?

   {{< record "The empty cover comes from …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Different First Page**: the first page gets its own header and footer,
   so the cover stays empty, and pages 2 and 3 keep the header and the
   numbers.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the steps in order: a header and numbers, but a clean cover.

   1. Type the header once, at the top of a page.
   2. Insert › Page Number › Bottom of Page.
   3. Tick Different First Page.
   4. Double-click in the text to go back.

   Why: You type the header once, add the numbers, keep the cover clean, then go back to the text.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A table of contents

**The idea:** Word makes the **table of contents** from the **heading
styles**: every heading with Heading 1 or Heading 2 is a line of it.
**References › Table of Contents** inserts it, with page numbers. After you
change, add or move a heading, click the contents and press **Update
Table**: Word does not update it by itself while you write.

**Aim:** make a table of contents, and keep it right after a change.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Click at the start of page 2. Choose **References › Table of Contents
   › Automatic Table 1**. Count the headings that it lists.

   {{< record "The contents list … headings, with …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **4 headings** (*When and where*, *What you can bring*, *How to swap a
   book*, *Prices*), each with its page number. The title is not in it: it
   has the style Title, not a heading style.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="4" unit="headings" hint="Count the lines with the style Heading 1."}
   The notice has four headings with Heading 1, and a title with Title. How
   many headings does the table of contents list?

   Why: The contents list the heading styles only: 4. The title has the style Title.
   :::

2. Change the heading *Prices* to *Book prices*. Look at the contents. Then
   click the contents, press **Update Table** and choose **Update entire
   table**.

   {{< record "Before Update Table … ; after …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Before: the contents still show **Prices**. After Update Table: they
   show **Book prices**. Word updates the contents only when you ask.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You changed a heading, and the contents still show the old name. What
   is the reason?

   - [x] Word does not update the contents by itself: press Update Table.

     Why: The contents change only when you update them.

   - [ ] The contents show only the first word of a heading.

     Why: They show the whole heading.

   - [ ] A heading can never change after the contents are made.

     Why: It can: then press Update Table.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/toc-builder.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/toc-builder.png" title="Contents Builder: headings, contents, update" >}}

3. In **Contents Builder**, give each heading Heading 1 or Heading 2, insert
   the contents, change a heading and press **Update Table**. Which style
   does *The questions*, a smaller heading under *Our survey*, get?

   {{< record "The questions gets …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Heading 2**: a smaller heading under a Heading 1. In the contents it
   is a line under *Our survey*, a little to the right.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which style does each line of the report get? Sort them.

   Heading 1
   :   Our survey

       Why: A main heading of the report.

   :   Conclusion

       Why: Another main heading.

   Heading 2
   :   The questions

       Why: A smaller heading under Our survey.

   Normal
   :   We asked 20 students about their phones.

       Why: A sentence of the text, not a heading.
   :::
